verdict: CME Group posted its best-ever third quarter — revenue up 13% to a record $1.7B — as volatile markets drove a record 29.4 million contracts a day across its exchanges.

kpis.label: Average daily volume
kpis.note: contracts a day — a Q3 record

segments.name: Clearing and transaction fees
segments.note: The toll on trades — fees for executing and clearing futures and options on CME's exchanges. Traders paid an average of $0.679 per contract.

segments.name: Market data and information services
segments.note: Selling the exchange's price data to banks, traders and data vendors — the fastest-growing line, at a record high.

segments.name: Other revenue
segments.note: Everything else — access and connectivity, co-location and other services.

flow.grossPlain: CME is an exchange, not a manufacturer — it has no cost-of-revenue line. Every cost of running the markets sits in operating expenses below, so revenue flows straight through to that step.

opex.name: Compensation & benefits
opex.note: Pay for the people who run the exchanges — the biggest cost, and slightly down YoY.

opex.name: Licensing & other fee agreements
opex.note: Fees CME pays for index licenses and partner agreements — up 28% YoY with volumes.

opex.name: Technology
opex.note: Running the trading systems, including the migration to cloud services.

opex.name: Amortization of purchased intangibles
opex.note: Spreading the cost of past acquisitions over their useful lives.

opex.name: Professional fees & outside services
opex.note: Outside legal, consulting and other services.

opex.name: Depreciation & amortization
opex.note: Spreading the cost of buildings, systems and equipment.

opex.name: Other expenses
opex.note: All remaining running costs. Shown $1M above the reported $62M so the rounded lines add exactly to reported totals (figures are rounded from tenths of $M).

otherDetail: Non-operating income was $213M as reported ($214M with rounding here): $1,418M of investment income — mostly interest earned for customers on collateral, which is largely passed back to them in the $1,264M of other non-operating expense — plus $103M of earnings from businesses CME part-owns, less $44M of interest and borrowing costs.
footerNote: CME reports no cost-of-revenue line, so — as with the Mastercard page — the flow starts from total revenue and every cost is an operating expense. CME reports in tenths of $M (revenue $1,737.3M, expenses $595.9M, operating income $1,141.4M, net income $1,036.9M); lines here are rounded to whole $M and adjusted by $1M where needed so the page ties exactly.
pngFooterNote: CME has no cost-of-revenue line; all costs are operating expenses.

takeaways.title: Record trading, in every asset class
takeaways.text: Average daily volume hit a Q3 record of 29.4 million contracts, with double-digit growth in all six product lines — interest rates (15.1M a day) and equity indexes (7.7M) are the giants. Uncertainty is good business for an exchange.

takeaways.title: Data is the quiet growth line
takeaways.text: Market data revenue hit a record $243M, up 20% — selling prices and data now brings in 14% of revenue and grows even when trading slows.

takeaways.title: A toll road's margins
takeaways.text: Operating income was $1,141M — 66 cents of every revenue dollar — because one more trade costs CME almost nothing to process. Net income rose 14% to $1,037M.

oneTimers: Adjusted results exclude the items in CME's reconciliation at the end of its release: on an adjusted basis operating income was $1.2B, net income $1.1B and EPS $3.02, vs GAAP EPS of $2.89.
